      "observations": [
        "All 86 changed paths and all hunks were read. This is a human-authored broad test assertion migration, not automation. Most changes map comparison operators to dedicated Assert methods; manifests receive sorting/spacing only. No production implementation changes. It is not strictly mechanical: the Calendar Edit assertion changes an assignment to a strict read comparison, so exclusion as formatter-only would discard a functional test correction.",
        "The historical Calendar test used Assert.ok((iframeDoc.querySelector(\"#item-title\").value = title),message), mutating the control and checking the assigned nonempty string. The patch checks the actual loaded value with strictEqual. The accepted test preserves that read-only comparison after dialog readiness changes.",
        "A parsed audit of all changed historical Assert calls checked 185 calls and found 91 calls without an explicit message; no parse failures. Exact locations and calls are in assertion-messages-3030.json. Comments and test names do not fill the message slot. This reports missing messages, not missing should alone. The custom fuzzy helper forwards its actual message parameter.",
        "Current Gecko dependency Assert receiver was checked at 8a7f5001d25b58d4799e19bfed316f872dcc739c: equal uses coercive equality, strictEqual uses strict equality, numeric comparison helpers reject non-number/non-Date operands. Its current lint mapping preserves operators and reports assignment separately without an autofix. Those dependency bytes and hashes are retained separately; no claim was made that current Gecko equals the 2025 dependency or the fixed comm revision.",
        "No broad production equality convention follows from this test patch. Current scalar and JSON-string assertions are evidence for their exact harness sections; they do not replace structural assertions by policy. No lint or tests were executed. Selected UI checks assert value/state; they do not verify rendered accessibility or timing.",
        "Complete Bug1974335 description/comments0–2 and D255230 creation-to-final timeline, all four submitted inline bodies and footer read. The bug has no description. Earlier77-ESLint-defect notice, later build completion and two Try links are historical reports tied to their own diffs; linked jobs were not opened and no lint/test run is claimed.",
        "The reviewer wonders whether JSON-string comparisons could use deepEqual and whether ok avoided large output. Actual landed session-store and repair-mbox hunks use Assert.equal on the JSON strings; deepEqual remains a suggestion, not an adopted structural-assertion policy. The manifest-order question is corrected by the reviewer to an existing alphabetical-order warning. The actual manifest moves test_ignoreSubscription.js into order.",
        "The Calendar Edit hunk is a functional assertion correction within the broad migration: the old assertion assigns title into the loaded input and checks the resulting nonempty string; the new strictEqual reads the input and compares it with title. The selected accepted test waits through its newer dialog helper and retains the read-only assertion. This can detect a wrong loaded title instead of overwriting the evidence. It does not independently verify Calendar save/persistence or rendered accessibility.",
        "SourceB read every hunk in all86 owned test/manifest paths and retained exact source proofs plus an185-call parsed assertion audit. The91 missing explicit message slots remain current-guidance deficiencies, independent of whether a message contains should. The custom fuzzy helper forwards its message argument; the migration does not turn failure-form messages or broad JavaScript equality choices into accepted global guidance."
      ],
